clinician.trajectory_summary: A 6-year-old girl with relapsed adrenal neuroblastoma after second-line cisplatin chemotherapy presented with febrile neutropenia progressing to persistent fever, abdominal pain and hepatosplenomegaly. Blood cultures revealed Candida species. Abdominal ultrasound identified hypoechoic nodular lesions in the spleen up to 2 cm, initially suspected to be tumor or Candida abscesses. PET/CT showed hypermetabolic splenic areas suggestive of inflammation but did not exclude tumor. Spleen tissue biopsy or splenectomy was ordered and performed. Histological analysis of the splenic tissue showed chronic inflammatory process consistent with candidiasis and no tumor cells were found, confirming splenic candidiasis as the cause of symptoms.
